sources.scopeNotes: A merchant’s account presented by this edition as first-century CE. Sections 4–6 describe the Adulis coastal trade network and an inland connection to the Auxumites. This supports reading context for Axum I, not a surveyed imperial boundary or a claim that Zoscales ruled the whole Axumite state. Ancient ethnic labels and the old translation’s language remain in the original, while guide prose uses place-based description. Coin origin and circulation totals are not supplied in section 6. The 1912 translation is retained as a historical edition, not presented as the latest critical text.

sources.scopeNotes: The digital transcript identifies its edition as the 1842 English translation. No individual translator is named by this item. The eight-page State Archives scan was visually read in full: its first page has no printed folio, followed by pp. 10–16. Relevant clauses match in substance, with editorial differences recorded in verification/hawaii-scan-review.json; the transcript is preserved rather than silently corrected. This constitutional text sets out norms in 1840, not proof of uniform enforcement or full-time office holding through the entire database phase. The supplied Polaris phase label and 1820–1898 bounds are preserved as dataset metadata, not a new assertion about the date the monarchy ended.
